relations.subject: n1ql:ansi-join

relations.subject: n1ql:lookup-join
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - deliberately NOT deprecatedIn. The page calls lookup join 'a legacy syntax' and dates its exclusive period to 4.1 and earlier, but it never says the syntax is deprecated, never names a removal version, and never tells the reader to stop using it. Asserting deprecatedIn here would be an invention. See version_finding - the gap between 'legacy' and 'deprecated' is the main vocabulary question this page raises
relations.evidence: A _lookup join_ is a legacy syntax for joins. It enables you to join a foreign key field on the left-hand side of the join with the primary [document key](../../learn/data/data.md#keys) on the right-hand side of the join. Couchbase Server version 4.1 and earlier supported only lookup joins.

relations.subject: n1ql:index-join
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - same predicate; here the object is the syntax it inverts, because the page gives index join no version boundary of its own, only 'another legacy syntax'. The asymmetry is faithful to the page: one legacy syntax is dated, the other is not
relations.evidence: An _index join_ is another legacy syntax for joins which reverses the direction of a lookup join.

relations.subject: n1ql:lookup-join
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - the registry has incompatibleWithCredentialType and incompatibleWithAccessSurface but nothing for two syntaxes that cannot co-occur in one statement. This is a syntax-level mutual exclusion and is the kind of constraint a query author hits at parse time
relations.evidence: Lookup joins can be chained with other lookup joins or nests and index joins or nests, but they cannot be mixed with ANSI joins, ANSI nests, or comma-separated joins.

relations.subject: n1ql:index-join

notable_absence.finding: This is the strongest deprecation-adjacent page in the batch and it still yields no deprecatedIn relation. Two whole join syntaxes are labelled '_a legacy syntax_' and '_another legacy syntax_', one of them is dated to 'Couchbase Server version 4.1 and earlier', both are documented at full length with syntax diagrams and multiple worked examples, and neither is anywhere called deprecated, marked for removal, or paired with a 'use X instead' instruction. The page therefore states an editorial judgement about age without stating a support commitment. I have recorded this as a minted documentedAsLegacy rather than stretching deprecatedIn to cover it. Reconciliation must decide whether the two are the same predicate; my view is that they are not, because deprecatedIn implies a version at which the deprecation took effect and a removal path, and 'legacy' as used here supplies neither. If the two are merged, this page will read as asserting that lookup joins were deprecated in 4.1, which is not what it says. Separately, and unlike insert.md, this page has no Security Requirements or RBAC section beyond one sentence, so it names no roles at all.

cross_component_finding: Three defects. (1) The USE NL Hint section's cross-reference points at the wrong anchor: 'refer to [Keyspace Hints](keyspace-hints.md#use-hash)' appears in BOTH the USE HASH section (line 627, correct) and the USE NL section (line 645, wrong - it should be #use-nl). The identical error is present in the Capella twin, so this is upstream in the shared source and will not be caught by any Server-versus-Capella comparison. (2) The privilege named here as `query_select` in code style is named _Query Select_ in italic title case on insert.md, and Authorization is where the reader is sent for both; one product, one privilege, two spellings across two adjacent reference pages. Any extraction keyed on surface form will produce two concepts. (3) The page depends on the Index Service for index joins ('requires an inverse index on the foreign key') and on the cost-based optimizer for join ordering, but declares neither as a service dependency in the way searchfun.md declares the Search Service; the dependency is only inferable from prose and links to cost-based-optimizer.md and the document-key page.
cross_product_finding: The largest and cleanest product divergence in this batch, and it runs in the direction the brief expected rather than the inverted direction the rest of my pages showed. The Server page carries an entire edition-gating apparatus that the Capella page does not have at all: the ENTERPRISE EDITION badge and its 'In Enterprise Edition ... the default method is hash' block, the COMMUNITY EDITION badge and its 'only nested-loop join is considered by the planner, and any specified `USE HASH` hint will be silently ignored' sentence, and the framing sentence 'Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition supports two join methods'. A grep of the Capella page for 'Enterprise' and 'Community' returns nothing. This is correct product behaviour - Capella has no Community Edition - and it means the Capella extraction record could not have found these facts, which explains why cloud/.../join.json contains no requiresEdition relation. It also means the CE join-method limitation exists in the corpus ONLY on the Server page, so an ontology built from Capella alone would silently lose it. The version gates diverge too: Server says 'In Couchbase Server 7.6 and later' where Capella says 'In clusters using Couchbase Server 7.6 and later' (the same fact, differently framed), and Server's two 6.5 statements and its '4.1 and earlier' sentence are absent from Capella entirely - Capella keeps the words 'a legacy syntax' but drops the version that dates it, leaving the reader with a pejorative and no timeframe. Finally, the Capella record captured only privileges and seeAlso links and missed the LATERAL 7.6 availableSince that IS present on its page; that is an extraction gap in the existing record, not a product difference, and reconciliation should backfill it.
version_finding: Four version boundaries harvestable here, spanning a wider range than any other page in this batch: 4.1 (lookup joins were once the only join syntax), 6.5 (ANSI join right-hand side widened to subqueries and generic expressions; outer joins internally rewritten to inner joins when the outer rows are filtered away), 7.6 (LATERAL keyword). Two vocabulary decisions follow. First, 'legacy' versus 'deprecated', discussed under notable_absence - do not conflate them. Second, this page needs a way to say 'version X and EARLIER', which every predicate in the registry currently lacks: 'Couchbase Server version 4.1 and earlier supported only lookup joins' is an upper-bounded fact, the mirror image of availableSince, and there is no availableUntil or supportedThrough to hold it. I have parked it in the object slot of documentedAsLegacy, which is the wrong shape and should be revisited. Third and most consequential for the ontology as a whole: this page proves that edition gating and version gating interact. Hash join is gated on Enterprise Edition, LATERAL is gated on 7.6 or later, and nothing in the model can express 'Enterprise Edition, 7.6 or later' as a single condition - two separate relations imply a conjunction the pages never actually state, and there is no way to record a feature that is EE-only in one version and universal in a later one. Worth deciding before the vocabulary is frozen.
